title: Non-blocking findings from PR #311's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #311 (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday), which returned needs_work for a separate, blocking issue: `_bars_to_frame`'s empty-bars branch returns a `RangeIndex` instead of an empty `DatetimeIndex`, crashing `_resample_to_target` with a raw `TypeError` whenever IBKR returns zero bars for a leg that also needs client-side resampling. That blocking issue is tracked on the parent task itself (its `review.comments`), not here -- this task collects only the findings that don't block merging once the blocking issue is fixed.

checklist.step: `get_intraday_bars_for_triple` fetches the `short_term` and `intermediate` legs sequentially even though they're independent IBKR HTTP calls (each potentially multi-page via `get_hourly_bars`'s own pagination). When both legs are `MINUTE`-unit, a caller pays roughly double the slower leg's latency for no correctness reason. Worth revisiting once a real caller exists (e.g. `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`) and the actual latency impact can be measured -- e.g. fetching both legs concurrently (a thread pool, since `IBKRProvider`'s HTTP calls are synchronous) if it turns out to matter in practice.

`_select_ibkr_bar_size`'s docstring is self-contradictory: its first sentence describes the return value as "the finest IBKR-supported bar interval that (a) is <= target_minutes and (b) evenly divides it," but the very next sentence and the actual implementation (`chosen_minutes = max(candidates)`) pick the *largest* (coarsest) evenly-dividing candidate, not the finest -- confirmed correct by the module's own '30-minute target fetches 5min not 1min' example one line later, and by the passing tests. No functional impact, but the wording would mislead a future reader trying to understand the selection rule from the docstring alone. Fix: reword the first sentence to say 'coarsest'/'largest' instead of 'finest'.

`DayTraderIntradayBars`/`get_intraday_bars_for_triple` never fetches or exposes a `long_term` leg even when it's configured as `MINUTE`-unit. `TimeframeTriple`'s ordering validation (`long_term > intermediate > short_term` by trading-minute length) doesn't prevent an all-intraday, scalping-style triple (e.g. long_term=100m/intermediate=25m/short_term=5m) from being persisted via `PUT /api/settings/trading-mode`. This matches PR #311's own task scope ('the short-term leg always; the intermediate leg too if it's also intraday'), so it wasn't a scope violation by that PR, but `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine` (the task expected to actually consume this module's output) should explicitly decide how to handle a fully-intraday triple -- either extend this module to also fetch `long_term` when it's `MINUTE`-unit, or document that this combination isn't supported yet -- before assuming IBKR-backed data is always available for whichever leg of the active triple needs it.

`_resample_to_target`'s open=first/high=max/low=min/close=last/volume=sum aggregation + `dropna(subset=[...])` pattern duplicates `StooqProvider._resample_weekly`'s identical aggregation logic almost verbatim (they differ only in the resample rule string, `"{n}min"` vs `"W-FRI"`). Could be extracted into one shared OHLCV-resampling helper (e.g. in `app.data.base`) to avoid the same logic living in two places, now that a second, deliberately-mirrored copy exists.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 3 (fetch/expose a `long_term` leg) was already fully resolved by PR #312 (`backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`), before this task was picked up -- `get_intraday_bars_for_triple` already calls `_fetch_leg` uniformly for `long_term`/`intermediate`/`short_term` on current `main`, confirmed by reading the module directly and by `TestGetIntradayBarsForTripleUnitScoping::test_all_three_legs_fetched_for_a_fully_intraday_triple` already passing. Marked done here rather than re-implemented, per `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.json`'s own checklist item 3, which explicitly named this exact bookkeeping gap and pointed at PR #312.
decisions.rationale: Re-implementing already-shipped behavior would be pure churn with no functional change and real risk of introducing a regression in code that's already covered by a passing, review-verified test suite; the task-board bookkeeping gap (this checklist item never having been ticked off) is the only thing that needed fixing, and doing so here (rather than waiting for someone to separately pick up the signal-engine-followups task's own pointer) closes the loop in one place.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 (sequential vs. concurrent leg fetching): implemented concurrent fetching. `get_intraday_bars_for_triple` now submits all three legs' `_fetch_leg` calls to a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3)` and blocks on every future's `.result()` before returning, rather than calling `_fetch_leg` three times in sequence.
decisions.rationale: A real caller now exists on `main` (`app.api.day_trader_signal.compute_day_trader_signal`, wired into `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` and `GET /api/watchlist` by PR #313) and it requires the active triple to be *fully intraday* (every leg `MINUTE`-unit, `_is_fully_intraday`) before it will even attempt a day-trader-mode signal -- so the three-sequential-IBKR-round-trips case this checklist item worried about isn't hypothetical anymore, it's the only case `compute_day_trader_signal` ever exercises. That makes this a genuine user-facing request-latency cost on two real HTTP endpoints (and, for `GET /api/watchlist`, multiplied once per watched ticker, since `_compute_signal` already calls `compute_day_trader_signal` per ticker sequentially -- a separate, larger pre-existing pattern this task doesn't touch, and a natural next place to look if watchlist-level latency ever needs its own follow-up). Each leg's fetch is fully independent (no shared mutable state, `IntradayLegResult`/`DayTraderIntradayBars` are frozen dataclasses, `_fetch_leg` doesn't mutate anything outside its own local scope), so fanning the three out to a thread pool and fanning back in via `.result()` is a low-risk, low-complexity way to collapse roughly 3x the slowest leg's IBKR round-trip latency down to roughly 1x, with no new synchronization surface. Rejected alternatives: (a) leaving it sequential, since the latency-sensitive real caller this checklist item was explicitly waiting for now exists and the fix is small; (b) `asyncio` instead of a thread pool, rejected because `IBKRProvider`'s HTTP calls (`urllib`-based, confirmed by reading `ibkr_provider.py`) are synchronous and this module/its callers (`app.api.day_trader_signal`, both routers) are themselves synchronous FastAPI path functions, not `async def` -- introducing asyncio here would mean either wrapping the whole call chain in `asyncio.to_thread`/`run_in_executor` anyway (no simpler than a plain `ThreadPoolExecutor`) or a much larger async-ification of code that has no other reason to become async. Verified the change is safe for the existing test suite's mocking convention (`mocker.create_autospec(IBKRProvider, instance=True)`, a `Mock`/`MagicMock`-based double whose call-recording is safe enough for this module's read-only, fixed-return-value usage under the GIL) by re-running the full suite rather than assuming it; one existing test (`test_non_composable_interval_resamples_from_finest_evenly_dividing_bar_size`) asserted `call_args_list[0].kwargs["bar_size"]`, which is no longer a valid assumption once leg-fetch order isn't guaranteed -- updated it to check bar_size membership across all calls instead of position.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4 (shared OHLCV-resampling helper): extracted `app.data.base.resample_ohlcv(frame, rule)`, implementing the open=first/high=max/low=min/close=last/volume=sum aggregation + incomplete-bin `dropna` + `index.name = "date"` pattern once. `StooqProvider._resample_weekly` now calls `resample_ohlcv(daily, "W-FRI")` and `app.data.day_trader_intraday._resample_to_target` now calls `resample_ohlcv(frame, f"{target_minutes}min")`, both losing their own previously-duplicated aggregation bodies.
decisions.rationale: The two implementations were byte-for-byte identical except for the resample rule string and (in `_resample_weekly`'s case only) an explicit `weekly.index.name = "date"` line after resampling -- `app.data.base` (already the shared home for `DataProvider`'s own OHLCV-shape contract/`ExtendedData`) was the natural place to put the extraction, per the task's own suggestion, rather than either provider module depending on the other. Setting `index.name = "date"` unconditionally in the shared helper (rather than only for the weekly case) is a no-op for `_resample_to_target`'s callers today (`_bars_to_frame` already names its `DatetimeIndex` `"date"`, and resampling preserves that name), so this doesn't change `day_trader_intraday.py`'s observed behavior, confirmed by the full test suite (including `TestSelectIbkrBarSizeAndResampling`'s existing resampling-shape assertions) passing unchanged.

comments.summary: Thread-safety check: `IBKRProvider.get_hourly_bars`'s call path (`_require_available` -> `get_gateway_status` -> `_request` -> `self._client.request`) touches only `self._base_url`/`self._client` (read-only for this path) -- it never reads/writes the two genuinely mutable instance attributes (`_scanner_params_cache`, `_last_scanner_run_at`), which belong exclusively to `get_scanner_params`/`run_scanner`, not `get_hourly_bars`. `httpx.Client` is documented safe for concurrent use from multiple threads. Combined with `IntradayLegResult`/`DayTraderIntradayBars` being frozen dataclasses and `_fetch_leg` never mutating outside its own local scope, the 3-way `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out has no shared-mutable-state hazard. Confirmed, not just assumed.

Exception handling under concurrency: `_fetch_leg` catches `IBKRUnavailableError` itself and returns a result value rather than raising, so the only way `get_intraday_bars_for_triple` propagates an exception is a genuinely unexpected one, which surfaces normally through `future.result()`; the `ThreadPoolExecutor` context manager's `__exit__` calls `shutdown(wait=True)` regardless of whether the `with` block exits via an exception, so every submitted future (including ones still running when the first exception is raised during the fan-in dict comprehension) is waited on before the exception propagates to the caller -- no orphaned/leaked background threads. Confirmed by reading `concurrent.futures`' documented context-manager semantics, not assumed.

`resample_ohlcv` extraction verified behavior-preserving for `StooqProvider._resample_weekly`: full `tests/unit/data/test_stooq_provider.py` suite (19 tests) re-run and passes unchanged, and the diff shows the extracted function is a byte-for-byte match of the original inline aggregation (including the `index.name = "date"` line, which the pre-extraction `_resample_to_target` never set but which is a no-op there since `_bars_to_frame` already names its `DatetimeIndex` `"date"`).

The one weakened test assertion (`test_non_composable_interval_resamples_from_finest_evenly_dividing_bar_size`, position -> membership check) doesn't lose meaningful coverage: given the test's own triple (long_term=1d, intermediate=100m -> "10min", short_term=25m -> "5min"), "5min" is only ever requested by the short_term leg, so `"5min" in bar_sizes_requested` is equivalent in practice to the original position-based check, and the very next assertion (`result.short_term.ibkr_bar_size == "5min"`) independently re-confirms the selection logic from the leg-result field regardless of what HTTP calls happened.

Independently re-ran the full backend suite (1341 passed, 100% line/branch coverage, `--cov-fail-under=90`), `ruff check .`, `mypy` (both clean), `python3 scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py` and `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` (both clean), `frontend` `yarn lint`/`yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (clean; frontend untouched by this PR, last-known state confirmed unaffected), and `backend/scripts/export_openapi.py` (no diff -- no API surface touched by this PR, matching the PR description). Also ran `tests/unit/data/test_day_trader_intraday.py` 15 additional times (10 solo + 5 as part of the earlier full-suite reruns) with no flake.

Non-blocking (tracked as a follow-up, not filed here as blocking): two remaining tests (`test_two_of_three_minute_unit_legs_are_fetched`, `test_all_three_legs_fetched_for_a_fully_intraday_triple`) assert on `provider.get_hourly_bars.call_count` under the new genuinely-concurrent fetch path. `unittest.mock.Mock.call_count`'s increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write that can lose updates under real thread concurrency (empirically confirmed: reliably undercounts at high call volume in the same test process, while `len(call_args_list)` stayed exact in every trial at every volume tested) -- but at this test's actual 2-3-calls-per-run scale, 0/20,000 trials reproduced a mismatch, so this is a theoretical robustness gap, not an observed or likely-in-practice flake.

Non-blocking (tracked as a follow-up, not filed here as blocking): `get_intraday_bars_for_triple`'s new `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out/fan-in block duplicates the same shape already used by `app/api/routers/stocks.py`'s indicator-history endpoint, with no shared helper -- the same class of duplication this PR's own `resample_ohlcv` extraction fixed elsewhere, though the two sites differ in one respect (stocks.py deliberately preserves a fixed error-priority resolution order that day_trader_intraday.py's version has no equivalent need for).

Non-blocking (tracked as a follow-up, not filed here as blocking): the newly-extracted `app.data.base.resample_ohlcv` has no direct unit test of its own -- only indirect coverage via its two current callers' existing tests.

review.notes: All four checklist items resolved correctly: (1) concurrent leg fetching is genuinely thread-safe (verified against IBKRProvider's real implementation, not assumed) and exceptions/futures are handled correctly by ThreadPoolExecutor's own context-manager semantics; (2) the docstring fix is accurate and resolves the prior self-contradiction; (3) the long_term-leg-already-fetched claim is correct, confirmed by diffing against the pre-PR-#312 code; (4) the resample_ohlcv extraction is behavior-preserving, confirmed by an isolated re-run of the Stooq provider's own test suite rather than trusting the full-suite pass alone. Full backend suite (1341 tests, 100% coverage), static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc), profit-target wording guard, and task-board validation all independently re-run and clean; no API surface touched so no OpenAPI snapshot regeneration was needed (confirmed via a no-diff re-export). No UI surface in this PR (pure backend data-layer change) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite steps don't apply, noted explicitly rather than silently skipped. Two non-blocking findings surfaced during independent verification beyond the PR's own stated scope (a subtle mock.call_count non-atomicity under concurrency, and a fan-out/fan-in pattern duplicated with app/api/routers/stocks.py) plus one from this reviewer's own pass (resample_ohlcv's lack of a direct unit test); all three filed on docs/tasks/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups-followups.json rather than left only in this PR's comments.
